$comment: P0-06 — the certified main-branch protection contract for the Bizosto ERP repository.
This file is the machine-readable half of docs/security/p0-06-github-main-protection.md.
scripts/verify-github-main-protection.mjs reads it and fails closed when the LIVE GitHub
ruleset no longer guarantees what is recorded here.
Every invariant below is DIRECTIONAL: the live configuration may be stronger than the
record, never weaker. That is what makes the record a ratchet rather than a snapshot.
It holds no credential. Everything it describes is readable anonymously from the public
repository, which is why the drift check needs no personal access token.
THIS IS THE ONE OPEN P0-06 CONTROL GAP, AND IT IS DELIBERATE.
The floor is the value the live ruleset may not drop below. The target is the value
P0-06 wants. They differ because on 2026-09-17 the repository had exactly ONE account
with any access at all - lacreativodesign, the owner, admin - and that account is the
author of every pull request. GitHub does not let a pull request author approve their
own pull request, so raising the live count to 1 today would not add a review: it would
make main permanently unmergeable, including for the pull request that would undo it.
So the count stays 0 until an independent reviewer exists. Closing the gap is a two-step
owner action, in this order, never the second alone:
1. grant a second human WRITE access to lacreativodesign/nextjs-boilerplate;
2. set required_approving_review_count to 1 AND set certifiedFloor to 1 here.
gapOpen is what keeps step 2 honest. The certification test refuses to let gapOpen go
false while certifiedFloor is still 0, so the gap cannot be closed on paper alone.
